title: VPC fundamentals — concept map
intro: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is your isolated network in AWS. You carve Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks into subnets per Availability Zone, attach an Internet Gateway for public ingress, and use NAT Gateway so private subnets reach the internet without inbound exposure. Route tables decide every packet hop. VPC DNS resolves internal names. Elastic IPs give stable public addresses; multi-AZ patterns tie it together for production.

conceptCards.title: CIDR & subnets
conceptCards.summary: Plan /16 VPC with /24 subnets per AZ. Public subnets have route to Internet Gateway; private subnets do not.

conceptCards.title: Internet Gateway
conceptCards.summary: Horizontally scaled VPC edge for bidirectional internet. Required for public subnets and NAT egress path.
conceptCards.example: ALB in public subnet with 0.0.0.0/0 → igw-xxxx

conceptCards.title: NAT Gateway
conceptCards.summary: Managed outbound-only internet from private subnets. Place in public subnet, one per AZ for HA.
conceptCards.example: Private EC2 pulls npm packages via NAT in same AZ

conceptCards.title: Route tables
conceptCards.summary: Longest-prefix match decides next hop. Each subnet associates with exactly one route table.

conceptCards.title: VPC DNS
conceptCards.summary: AmazonProvidedDNS at VPC CIDR+2 resolves internal hostnames and AWS service endpoints.
conceptCards.example: EnableDnsHostnames for public DNS names on instances with public IPs

conceptCards.title: Elastic vs ephemeral IP
conceptCards.summary: Elastic IP persists across stop/start; ephemeral public IP changes unless Elastic IP associated.
conceptCards.example: NAT Gateway requires Elastic IP allocation in public subnet

conceptCards.title: Multi-AZ VPC patterns
conceptCards.summary: Mirror public/private subnets per AZ, NAT per AZ, ALB cross-zone, databases Multi-AZ.
conceptCards.example: Three AZs × (public + private) + three NAT Gateways
